10.1002_adfm.202518725: Cu‐based covalent organic framework (COF) catalysts with well‐defined and porous structures hold significant promise for CO 2 electroreduction reaction (CO 2 RR), while producing mainly simple C1 products. Designing Cu‐based COF catalysts targeting C2+ products are still challenging due to unfavorable C─C coupling on far‐located isolated Cu sites. Herein, vinylene‐linked metal‐covalent organic frameworks (MCOFs,Cu‐CTU+TMTT‐MCOF and Cu‐CTU+TMTP‐MCOF) catalysts with a well‐defined crystalline structure, high density, and symmetrical Cu triatomic coordination environment are elaborately constructed. The Cu‐CTU+TMTT‐MCOF demonstrated a remarkable CO 2 RR‐to‐C 2 H 4 faradaic efficiency (FE) of 51.9% and a current density of 360.1 mA cm −2 at the potential of −1.17 V versus reversible hydrogen electrode (RHE) in 1.0 m KOH solution. In situ Fourier transform infrared spectra and density functional theory studies revealed that the adjacent symmetric Cu site with a close distance in vinylene‐linked MCOFs can stabilize H 2 COH‐H 2 C * intermediates, thus improving the selectivity of C2 products. This study presents an innovative approach for constructing symmetrical Cu triatomic sites while offering critical guidance for advancing metal‐based COFs to enhance CO 2 RR‐to‐C 2 H 4 efficiency.
10.1002_advs.75152: The electrochemical reduction of CO 2 to formic acid (HCOOH), a valuable chemical feedstock, offers a promising pathway toward carbon neutrality. However, achieving high selectivity, industrial current densities, long‐time stability, and the direct production of pure products simultaneously remains difficult. Here we present tensile‐strained bismuth nanosheets (TS‐BiNs) created through a scalable mechanochemical ball‐milling and carbonation process, effectively addressing all of these challenges. The TS‐BiNs catalyst demonstrates outstanding performance, maintaining over 92% Faradaic efficiency for HCOO − across a wide current density range from −50 to −1000 mA cm −2 and an excellent stability at −100 mA cm −2 for over 100 h. When used in a solid‐state electrolyte reactor (4 cm 2 ), it ensures the continuous and stable production of pure HCOOH solutions with widely adjustable concentrations (40–1500 m M ) at 400 mA over 100 h. Combined experimental and theoretical analyses reveal that the tensile strain enhances the adsorption of the * OCHO intermediate and inhibits the competing hydrogen evolution reaction, thereby directing the process toward highly efficient HCOOH formation. This work underscores the significant potential of strain engineering in catalyst design and introduces an integrated catalyst‐reactor strategy for practical electrochemical CO 2 upgrading.
10.1002_eem2.70402: Sodium metal batteries are promising candidates for large‐scale energy storage due to their low cost and high energy density. However, the repeated formation and disruption of the solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) on the sodium anode significantly limits their long‐term cycling stability. Here, we propose a targeted SEI repair strategy using an ester‐ether hybrid solvation electrolyte. By confining reactive trimethyl phosphate (TMP) within a solvation shell dominated by diethylene glycol ether (G2), this design mitigates direct sodium anode corrosion by free TMP while simultaneously directing the preferential decomposition of solvated TMP at SEI defect sites, enabling rapid SEI restoration. Microstructural analysis confirms the formation of a robust composite SEI, rich in NaF and Na 3 PO 4 , which effectively suppresses dendrite growth due to its excellent mechanical integrity and high ionic conductivity. As a result, the Na||Na 3 V 2 (PO 4 ) 3 cell with this electrolyte exhibits enhanced cycling performance, retaining 90% capacity after 4500 cycles at 1 C and 98.5% after 950 cycles at 20 C. Furthermore, a pouch cell demonstrates the practical viability of this approach, delivering a stable specific capacity of 109.47 mAh g −1 after 350 cycles at 3 C and highlighting its potential for high‐performance sodium metal batteries.
10.1016_j.solener.2026.114474: In this study, we propose and compare two fully solar-powered desalination systems designed to enhance the Recovery Ratio (RR) and valorize the brine produced by a Reverse Osmosis (RO) unit. To achieve these goals, both systems integrate thermal and electrical energy storage and include Membrane Distillation (MD) units operating in series with the RO unit. The first configuration (System A) is powered by photovoltaic (PV) panels and solar thermal (ST) collectors, while the second (System B) combines hybrid photovoltaic/thermal (PV/T) panels with ST collectors. The systems are modeled and simulated under real meteorological conditions over a full year of operation in Almería, Spain.The RO-MD tandem improves both RR and freshwater output compared to RO alone. System A shows a 9.22% production increase over RO alone, and System B shows 8.60%. RR rises from 40.50% to 44.23% in System A, and from 42.04% to 45.66% in System B.Using PV/T in System B enhances performance: seawater preheating boosts RR of RO, lowers specific energy consumption (SEC), and improves PV efficiency, resulting in reduced energy use, higher output, and longer operation. This yields an 8.93% production gain and a 3.24% RR increase respect to System A.LCOW values are 5.01 and 5.27\,USD/m3 for Systems B and A, respectively. Though higher than conventional freshwater costs, they are lower than many reported for solar-powered desalination systems.
10.1039_d5ta06995e: This work reports a self-supporting high-entropy spinel oxide (FeNiCoMnCr) 3 O 4 electrode, whose abundant oxygen vacancies promote OER intermediates adsorption and reduce energy barrier of the *O formation step, showing the excellent OER performance.
